subject: Polity
description: Chief Justice of India (CJI) — appointment, retirement, powers, master of roster, recent CJIs, role in Supreme Court collegium.

questions.stem: The Chief Justice of India is APPOINTED by:

options.option_text: The Vice President of India alone

questions.explanation: Article 124(2): The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the PRESIDENT under his hand and seal. CONVENTION: the SENIOR-MOST judge of the Supreme Court is appointed CJI (the 'seniority principle'). The outgoing CJI traditionally recommends the next in line. KEY EVENT: Supersession Crisis 1973 — Indira Gandhi's govt SUPERSEDED 3 senior judges (J.M. Shelat, K.S. Hegde, A.N. Grover) to appoint A.N. Ray as CJI — sparking outrage that the seniority convention had been broken. Result: collegium system gradually emerged via judicial decisions (Three Judges Cases, 1981, 1993, 1998). MEMORANDUM OF PROCEDURE: outlines the CJI appointment process — currently being reviewed by NJAC (National Judicial Appointments Commission, struck down by SC in 2015). RETIREMENT AGE: 65 years (Article 124(2)(b)). RECENT CJIs: D.Y. Chandrachud (Nov 2022 - Nov 2024), Sanjiv Khanna (Nov 2024 - May 2025), B.R. Gavai (May 2025 onwards) — first Buddhist-Dalit CJI of India. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'who appoints CJI' is a SSC, UPSC, polity 1-mark guarantee.

questions.stem: What is the RETIREMENT AGE for a Supreme Court judge (including CJI)?
questions.explanation: Article 124(2)(b): Supreme Court judges retire at AGE 65. HIGH COURT JUDGES retire at AGE 62 (Article 217(1)). DON'T CONFUSE — quick retirement-age table: SC Judges: 65; HC Judges: 62; Comptroller-Auditor-General (CAG): 65; UPSC Chairman/Member: 65; Election Commission of India members: 65 (or 6 yrs, whichever earlier); Lokpal: 70; CVC/CIC: 65 (or 5 yrs term). PROPOSALS to RAISE retirement age: there's been periodic debate about raising HC age to 65 (matching SC) — would help reduce pendency by retaining experienced judges. NOT YET enacted. POST-RETIREMENT: SC judges often serve in tribunals, commissions of inquiry, arbitration boards. Some controversy about 'post-retirement plums' for cooperative judges (e.g., chairing the Press Council, Law Commission, NHRC). NOTABLE: under Article 128, the President can recall a retired SC judge to TEMPORARILY hear cases — used rarely. PYQ FREQUENCY: SC vs HC retirement ages is a top-3 polity confusion — 1-2 Qs per cycle in CGL, UPSC. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise constitutional ages.

questions.stem: The CJI is described as the 'MASTER OF THE ROSTER' because he/she:

options.option_text: Allocates cases to Supreme Court benches
Manages the SC's payroll alone (option here)

questions.explanation: MASTER OF THE ROSTER — administrative power of the CJI to ALLOCATE CASES to specific benches and judges. This is exclusive prerogative; no judge can decide his own case-bench composition. ROSTER PRACTICE: CJI publishes a 'subject-roster' assigning categories (criminal, constitutional, tax, environment, etc.) to specific judges. JUSTICE J. CHELAMESWAR PRESS CONFERENCE (12 Jan 2018): four senior-most SC judges (Chelameswar, Gogoi, Lokur, Kurian Joseph) PUBLICLY criticized then-CJI Dipak Misra over allegations of biased case-assignments — historic event in Indian judiciary. SC subsequently affirmed (Asok Pande v. SC of India, 2018) that 'master of roster' is the CJI's settled prerogative — but with constitutional accountability. ANALOGUE: HC Chief Justices have similar roster power for their courts. ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS of CJI: (1) Roster allocation. (2) Constituting Constitution Benches (5+ judges). (3) Convening Full Court meetings. (4) Heading the Collegium for HC/SC judge appointments. (5) Heading the SC administration. PYQ ANGLE: 'master of roster' is a top UPSC, IIBF/ICAI legal-section MCQ.

questions.answer_source: Asok Pande v. SC of India 2018

questions.stem: In the COLLEGIUM SYSTEM, the CJI heads a body that recommends:

options.option_text: Salary increases for the SC alone

questions.explanation: COLLEGIUM SYSTEM — judicial body of senior judges that RECOMMENDS appointments, elevations, and transfers of HC and SC judges to the President. EVOLUTION VIA THREE JUDGES CASES: 1ST JUDGES CASE (1981) — 'consultation' by President meant only consultation, not concurrence with CJI. 2ND JUDGES CASE (1993) — CJI's opinion has primacy; need consultation with 2 senior-most SC judges. 3RD JUDGES CASE (1998) — collegium = CJI + 4 senior-most SC judges (for SC appointments). FOR HC APPOINTMENTS: CJI + 2 senior-most SC judges + HC Chief Justice + 2 senior-most HC judges. NJAC v. COLLEGIUM (2015): SC struck down 99th Constitutional Amendment that would have replaced collegium with NJAC (govt + judges + civil society) — restoring collegium as supreme. CRITICISMS of collegium: lack of transparency, no formal selection criteria, accusations of nepotism. 2024-25 CJI Khanna initiative: publicizing collegium reasoning more transparently. REMOVAL of JUDGES is a SEPARATE process (Article 124(4)) — by President via PARLIAMENTARY IMPEACHMENT (special majority + addressing both houses on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity'). PYQ FREQUENCY: collegium concepts are tested in UPSC, judicial-services exams.

questions.stem: Who was the FIRST WOMAN judge of the Supreme Court of India?

options.option_text: Justice Ruma Pal alone alone (option here)

questions.explanation: JUSTICE M. FATHIMA BEEVI was appointed to the Supreme Court of India in OCTOBER 1989 — the FIRST WOMAN to hold this position. She served until April 1992. BACKGROUND: born 1927 in Pathanamthitta, Kerala; first woman to top the Bar Council Examination in India; Kerala HC judge before SC elevation. She later served as Governor of Tamil Nadu (1997-2001). MILESTONES IN INDIAN WOMEN JUDICIARY: (1) Anna Chandy — first woman HIGH COURT judge (Kerala HC, 1959). (2) Fathima Beevi — first woman SC judge (1989). (3) Justice R. Banumathi (2014-2020) — second woman after Fathima Beevi to retire. (4) Justice Indira Banerjee (2018-2022). (5) Justice Hima Kohli, B.V. Nagarathna, Bela Trivedi (all elevated 2021). NOTABLE: B.V. Nagarathna is set to become the FIRST WOMAN CHIEF JUSTICE OF INDIA (Sept 2027 - Oct 2027 tenure of ~1 month). REPRESENTATION: only ~11% of HC judges are women; 4 women SC judges as of 2025. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'firsts' in judiciary appear in CGL, UPSC, IBPS GA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Who was the FIRST CHIEF JUSTICE OF INDIA after the Constitution came into force?
questions.explanation: JUSTICE H.J. KANIA (Harilal Jekisundas Kania) was the FIRST CJI of India, sworn in on 26 January 1950 — the day the Constitution came into force. Tragically, he died in office on 6 November 1951 — the only CJI to have died while in office. BACKGROUND: born 1890 in Ahmedabad; Bombay HC judge before being elevated. CHRONOLOGY OF FIRST FEW CJIs (memorize for UPSC): (1) H.J. Kania — 1950-1951. (2) M. Patanjali Sastri — 1951-1954. (3) Mehr Chand Mahajan — 1954. (4) B.K. Mukherjea — 1954-1956. (5) Sudhi Ranjan Das — 1956-1959. CURRENT CJI (April 2026): B.R. Gavai (sworn in May 2025; retires Nov 2025). FIRSTS: Indian-origin CJI: Justice K.G. Balakrishnan (Dalit, 2007-2010); Justice Ranganath Misra (1990-91, longer tenure ~ 2 years). LONGEST-SERVING CJI: Justice Y.V. Chandrachud (1978-1985, ~7 years 3 months — record). SHORTEST: Justice K.N. Singh (just 17 days, Nov 1991). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'first CJI' is a perennial UPSC, CGL fact.

questions.stem: Who can act as CJI in the absence of the CJI (e.g., during illness or foreign visit)?

options.option_text: Senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
Chief Justice of Delhi HC alone.

questions.explanation: Article 126: When the office of CJI is VACANT (between resignations) or when CJI is absent or otherwise unable to perform duties (illness, foreign visit, leave), the President may appoint a JUDGE of the Supreme Court — by convention, the SENIOR-MOST judge — to act as CJI. PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: when CJI Sanjiv Khanna was on leave in 2025, the next senior-most judge presided over Court 1 in his absence. ARTICLE 127 (Ad-hoc judges): if there's a quorum problem at SC, the CJI (with President's prior consent) can request a HIGH COURT judge to sit as 'ad-hoc' SC judge — used rarely (e.g., Justice U.U. Lalit's elevation through this route). ARTICLE 128 (Recall retired judges): the CJI can request retired SC/HC judges (with their consent + President's permission) to sit as judges of the SC for SPECIFIC cases — used for high-profile constitutional benches. INTERESTING: Acting CJI carries the same powers as a full CJI but only for the duration of acting tenure; doesn't count toward retirement age extension. PYQ ANGLE: Articles 126, 127, 128 appear in UPSC CSE, HJS exams.
